Hedric Ashby.narrative: I keep the wood edge for the Ashby fields, and I know every snare line on it by heart. Last week I found my best line cut and emptied, and I know whose boots have been on that path — Coldwell boots, and Hob Ferrier's besides. Osbert tells me to let it lie and keep the peace; I say a man who lets his snares be taken will lose his fields next. I carry my bow on the edge now, and I mean to have what is mine back or its worth in marks.
values: a debt unpaid is an insult
goals: Get back my snares or their value from the Coldwell people
Prove Hob Ferrier sold my hides at Ferncross
Keep the wolves and the outlaws off the Ashby fields
See Wren safe and taught to shoot straight
Teach Wren to draw and loose a bow true enough to trust her at the edge
Make a bow of his own from a stave he's been seasoning since last winter

relations.name: Osbert Ashby
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He took me in and fed me; I wish he would take my side against Coldwell as readily.

relations.name: Wren Ashby
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She is the whole of what I am keeping the wood edge for.

relations.name: Edith Ashby
relations.label: good-sister
relations.note: She keeps a good table and asks no questions about the hides I bring in.

relations.name: Roland Ashby
relations.label: nephew
relations.note: A steady lad, but he ploughs where I would hunt.

relations.name: Beorn Beornson
relations.label: friend
relations.note: The only man who reads a trail the way I do.

relations.name: Hob Ferrier
relations.label: thief
relations.note: He was at Ferncross with hides that had my snare-cuts in them.

relations.name: Ned Hale
relations.label: outlaw
relations.note: His people cut my line and emptied it; he can deny it to the Reeve.

relations.name: Marta Hale
relations.label: outlaw
relations.note: She leads them and she knows what her brother does on the road.

relations.name: Hal Tolley
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: A Guild tenant with a barn, and no more sense of the woods than a sheep.

memories.gist: I found my best snare line cut and empty near the Coldwell boundary, the wire coiled and taken.
At Ferncross market I saw Hob Ferrier with a bundle of hides, and one had the notch of my own knife in it.
Beorn Beornson and I tracked a wolf pair along the wood edge all one cold morning and took both.
When the Lean Year came I brought in enough venison that the Ashby table never went short.
Wren asked me to teach her the bow, and I cut her a small one from a hazel stave.

stances.why: A snare line is a man's work and his meat; to cut it is to steal twice over.
Since the snare was cut I will not walk the wood edge unarmed.
They took from me and the Reeve does nothing; someone must make them answer.
Osbert is my brother and I will not shame him at his own table, whatever I think of his softness.
A girl who knows the paths and the bow will never be at a stranger's mercy.

Hedric Ashby.secret: I have gone once to the Coldwell boundary at dusk with my bow, meaning to make Ned Hale speak to me, and came away without knocking. I have told no one, not even Osbert.
pastimes: Walking his snare lines at first light, reading the ground for tracks
Shooting at a mark on the field edge until his arm aches
Sitting at the Ashby hearth mending snares and bowstrings while Wren watches
Hedric Ashby.calling: I keep the wood edge and the snare lines on it, and I'd sooner be out on that edge than anywhere under a roof.

Wren Ashby.narrative: I live in the Ashby house with my father and my uncle's family, and I know the hens by name and the way to the wood edge by heart. Father lets me carry his spare bowstring and sometimes his snares, and I am learning to set them without tangling. Nell Tolley is my friend though she is afraid of the woods, and I tell her there is nothing in them worse than a wolf, and Father can shoot a wolf.
values: the hens must be fed before me
be brave at the wood edge
goals: Learn to set a snare as well as Father does
Make Nell Tolley not afraid of the woods
See the snare line that was cut and find out who did it
Set a snare all by herself that catches something
Get Nell Tolley to walk to the wood edge with her, just once

relations.name: Hedric Ashby
relations.label: father
relations.note: He knows every path and he is never afraid, and he is teaching me the bow.

relations.name: Osbert Ashby
relations.label: uncle
relations.note: He is kind and gives me bread with honey when the hens have laid well.

relations.name: Edith Ashby
relations.label: aunt
relations.note: She lets me help with the hens and does not scold when I drop an egg.

relations.name: Tib Tolley
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: He is older and knows the fields, and he tells me stories about the barn watch.

relations.name: Nell Tolley
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She is afraid of the woods, so I hold her hand when we play near them.

memories.gist: Father cut me a small hazel bow and showed me how to stand sideways to the target.
I helped Aunt Edith gather the eggs and only broke one, and she laughed instead of scolding.
Nell Tolley cried at the edge of the woods and I told her Father would shoot any wolf that came.

stances.why: He knows the woods and the bow and he says the outlaws took his snares.
Nell is afraid, so someone must not be.
Aunt Edith says the hens pay for the bread.

pastimes: Feeding and naming the hens, and chasing them back into the coop
Practising with a little bow Father cut for her at a straw mark
Following the wood edge path as far as she dares before turning back
Wren Ashby.calling: I want to be a wood-edge keeper like Father, and know every snare line by heart, and never be afraid out there.
